## Overview

This program creates a treatment-level summary of analysis population membership. It uses simulated subject-level data with twice the original sample size and reports counts and percentages for the Intent-to-Treat, Safety, and Per-Protocol Analysis Sets.

## Analysis Steps

1. Construct the original five-subject source structure and duplicate complete subject records to create ten simulated subjects.
2. Retain randomized subjects using `RANDFL = "Y"` and assign records to the planned treatment group.
3. Add an overall Total record for each randomized subject.
4. Create complete treatment and analysis-set combinations so that zero-count categories remain in the output.
5. Count subjects in the Intent-to-Treat, Safety, and Per-Protocol Analysis Sets.
6. Calculate percentages using the number of randomized subjects within each treatment group as the denominator.
7. Transpose the results into treatment columns and generate the Excel and formatted RTF/PDF outputs.

## ADaM Data and Main Variables

The analysis uses the subject-level ADaM dataset **ADSL**.

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `USUBJID` | Unique subject identifier |
| `TRT01PN` | Numeric planned treatment used to create treatment columns |
| `RANDFL` | Randomized population flag and denominator definition |
| `SAFFL` | Safety Analysis Set flag |
| `FASFL` | Full Analysis Set flag retained in the simulated ADSL structure |
| `PPROTFL` | Per-Protocol Analysis Set flag |

The displayed Intent-to-Treat Analysis Set is derived from randomized subjects, while all percentages use randomized treatment-group totals as denominators.
